# Index types — vocabulary

- **partial index** · hyponym — The `where` argument allows you to define [partial indexes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-partial.html) (also known as filtered indexes). A partial index only includes rows that match a specified condition, which reduces the index size and improves both write performance and query  · aka: partial indexes, filtered index, partialIndexes — https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/indexes#configuring-partial-indexes-with-where-configuring-partial-indexes-with-where

- **GIN index** · hyponym — <Info> Note: `USING gin` specifies that this is a GIN index. The extension allows `column1` (text), `column2` (integer), and `column3` (timestamp) to be indexed efficiently using GIN. </Info> · aka: GIN, GIN indexes, generalized inverted index, gin_trgm_ops · Postgres — https://thenile.dev/docs/extensions/btree_gin#creating-a-gin-index-with-btree-gin
- **GiST index** · hyponym — GiST indexes are a versatile type of index that can handle complex data types, such as geometric shapes, full-text search, and network addresses. [They are implemented using a custom data structure optimized for searching large amounts of data1](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/gist.html). He · aka: GiST, SP-GiST, GiST indexes, btree_gist · Postgres — https://thenile.dev/docs/postgres/indexes#gist-index

- **vector index** · hyponym · aka: vector indexes, HNSW, IVFFlat, DiskANN, vectorIndex, approximate nearest neighbor · pgvector / Atlas Vector Search / Convex vector index — an index type, not the Pinecone sense
- **multikey index** · hyponym · aka: multikey, multikey indexes

- **wildcard index** · hyponym — If a field is an embedded document or array (like `attributes.size`), the wildcard index recurses into the field and indexes all embedded scalar field values. · aka: wildcard indexes — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields/#results

- **clustered index** · hyponym · aka: clustered indexes, clustered collection, WITHOUT ROWID
- **expression index** · hyponym — An expression index stores the result of an expression rather than a raw column value. Use expression indexes when queries frequently filter or sort by a computed value. · aka: expression indexes, functional index, index on an expression — https://docs.turso.tech/sql-reference/statements/create-index#expression-indexes
